answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a marble tile set into a shared floor: one tile is cheap, but paving a garden of thousands of fake identities costs a fortune, because each stake is locked for a season and slashed if the identity is caught misbehaving. A single honest agent pays almost nothing beyond the temporary lockup, while an attacker must fund every fake, and each detected fake burns its stake, its pigment struck from the shared record. The bond makes identity expensive to forge and cheap to keep honest.
